sections.h2: What is the fastest way to sell a house in Kearny, NJ?
sections.html:
A cash sale is the fastest route in Kearny, because it avoids the buyer's mortgage commitment and appraisal, and a listing is the slowest and usually the highest-priced. Whichever you choose, the town's certificate of occupancy inspection can set your closing date, since the construction office schedules those visits only on select days.

Kearny is a Hudson County town of 40,862 people by the Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate, 2.7% below the 2020 base of 42,004. Only 42.9% of housing units are owner-occupied, so a good share of Kearny sellers are landlords as well as homeowners, and a few own buildings with tenants.

sections.h2: How is Kearny laid out, and where did its housing come from?
sections.html:
Kearny sits on a peninsula between two rivers: the Passaic separates it from Newark and Belleville, and the Hackensack separates it from Secaucus and Jersey City. The town has 8.84 square miles of land and about 4,749 people per square mile, and it splits into three areas: the Kearny Uplands, the Kearny Meadows and South Kearny, where the two rivers meet.

The housing grew out of mills. Clark Thread opened its Kearny plants in 1875, and Nairn Linoleum followed in 1887, drawing Scottish workers who also gave the town its soccer reputation. Cargo ships were built at the Kearny yards in World War I and warships in World War II, and Western Electric's Kearny Works, opened in 1928, employed as many as 24,000 people. Population rose from 777 in 1880 to 40,716 in 1930, so much of the older housing dates from that surge.

  • Main streets include Kearny Avenue, Bergen Avenue, Midland Avenue, Schuyler Avenue and Passaic Avenue.
  • Riverbank Park, Bunnyland Hill and West Hudson Park (shared with Harrison) are the largest green spaces.
  • The Kearny Public Library, a Carnegie library, houses a local museum on its third floor.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Kearny buyers and sellers?
sections.html:
Kearny is a mostly renting town where 45.0% of residents were born abroad and 65.2% speak another language at home. Median household income is $79,154, and the median home value is $459,400.

sections.h2: How do roads, buses and schools affect a Kearny sale?
sections.html:
Buyers who commute to Manhattan or Newark will look at the road network first. The Belleville Turnpike (Route 7) runs along the northern border, Kearny Avenue continues into Route 17 as Ridge Road, U.S. 1/9 and the Pulaski Skyway pass through, and Interstate 280 ends at the New Jersey Turnpike at the Exit 15W tollgate. NJ Transit buses reach the Port Authority Bus Terminal and Newark on the 1, 30, 40 and 76 routes. Passenger service on the old Newark Branch ended in October 1966, and the Arlington station is abandoned.

The Kearny School District had 5,142 students in seven schools in 2021-22: Franklin, Garfield, Roosevelt, Schuyler and Washington elementary schools, Lincoln Middle School and Kearny High School. Hudson Arts and Science Charter School operates two campuses in town.

sections.h2: What paperwork does Kearny require before you close?
sections.html:
Kearny's Construction Code Enforcement Department handles it, and it posts a residential certificate of occupancy package that includes a checklist, an application, and the one- and two-family smoke and carbon monoxide detector compliance form. The office is open Monday through Friday, 8 to 4, at (201) 955-7880. It warns that certificate inspections happen only on select days and that last-minute inspections right before closing cannot be accommodated, so book well ahead.

  • A zoning permit costs $25 and is required in almost every case before a construction permit can be issued.
  • A building subcode construction permit costs $20 per $1,000 of listed work, with a $50 minimum.
  • Processing usually takes 5 to 7 business days, and the office has up to 20 working days to issue a permit.

These numbers matter if the house has unfinished work. A garage conversion or an addition done without permits is the kind of gap a buyer's attorney will ask about.

sections.h2: Can buyers or investors rent a Kearny house short term?
sections.html:
Not in a single-family house. Section 15-4 of the Town Code, which grew out of Ordinance 2017-61, restricts short-term rentals of single-family homes, and at its February 10, 2026 meeting the Town Council took up an amendment that would apply the ban to any single- or multi-family dwelling, define a short-term rental as less than 30 consecutive days, and bar advertising or facilitating one. The draft sets fines of $750 per day for a first violation. Ask the town clerk whether it has been adopted before you promise a buyer short-term income.

Rental owners also deal with lead inspections for rental dwelling units, and the town posts an application for filing lead-safe or lead-free certificates. If you sell a building with tenants, collect those certificates and the state landlord registration form for the buyer.

  • Seniors, disabled residents and veterans can claim property tax relief through forms posted on the town website.
  • The tax collector can supply a redemption statement for $20 and a duplicate bill for $5.
  • Kearny adds a 6% year-end penalty when delinquencies exceed $10,000 by June 30, the end of the fiscal year.

sections.h2: What do Kearny sellers pay in transfer fees and taxes?
sections.html:
The seller owes New Jersey's realty transfer fee, and the state schedule applied to Kearny's $459,400 median value gives roughly $3,800. The deed for a Kearny house is recorded with Hudson County, so your closing agent will file there. For taxes, call the tax collector at (201) 955-7888, in the lower level of Town Hall and open 9 to 4 on weekdays, for the current balance and the next installment.

A building with tenants adds paperwork: lead certificates, the landlord registration and any rental inspection records, to go along with the smoke alarm certificate. A cash buyer who takes the property as it stands can skip repair negotiations, though the certificate and any open permits still have to be settled.

faqs.q: How long does a Kearny certificate of occupancy inspection take to schedule?
faqs.a: There is no fixed wait, because the construction office schedules those inspections only on select days as availability permits. It advises leaving significant time before closing and says it cannot fit in last-minute inspections. Call (201) 955-7880 as soon as you have a contract.

faqs.q: Does Kearny require a smoke and carbon monoxide certificate when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes for a one- or two-family house. State fire code requires the compliance certificate before a sale, and Kearny's residential certificate package includes the application. The certificate is valid for six months.

faqs.q: Can I rent my Kearny house on a short-term basis?
faqs.a: Section 15-4 restricts short-term rentals of single-family homes, and an amendment taken up on February 10, 2026 would extend the ban to every dwelling and start fines at $750 a day. Ask the town clerk which version is in force.

faqs.q: Who pays New Jersey's realty transfer fee in Kearny?
faqs.a: The seller pays it when the deed is recorded in Hudson County. The rate rises in bands with the price, and sales above $1 million add a graduated percent fee. Your closing agent will compute it.

faqs.q: What happens to Kearny taxes at closing?
faqs.a: Ask the tax collector for the current balance and, if any lien exists, a redemption statement, which costs $20. Confirm there are no older balances before you set a closing date.
